entry.title: Saturn
entry.summary: saturn - daniel daum's personal website, a minimalist redesign built with html and css
entry.content:
This is the project page for my personal website, this website - called saturn.

I have never been completely satisfied with the look of my website. I've always been drawn to simple, minimal pages, but I've struggled to find a design that feels entirely my own. In my efforts to improve the things I didn’t like, I’ve remade this site several times until its become what is is today: my cozy minimal personal website.

Under the hood, the implementation is deliberately kept simple: static HTML and CSS, no JavaScript framework, and a domain registered and hosted on Cloudflare. I write HTML and CSS locally on my machine, when changes hit main a CI pipeline pushes them to Cloudflare Pages.

I chose the name Saturn because it's my favorite planet. It has rings!

Evolution | version history

Feeling nostalgic, I decided to go through the previous evolutions of my site's design. Easy to do since the entire history of the website (back to my first commit in 2021) exists in this repository.

I like food and building stuff (Nov 2021)

This was my first website, two days after my first commit. It had one HTML file and one stylesheet, used Lato from Google Fonts, and was hosted on GitHub Pages. At the time, I was learning how to write HTML and CSS, figuring out how hosting worked, and trying to decide what a personal site should be. I remember feeling proud that I had a website, and proud that I built it myself. I still feel proud.

create-react-app (Jan 2022)

You know what proves you're a real software engineer? Rebuilding your static four-page website in React. I remember thinking at the time, "Oh yeah, baby! This is what real developers do." It used React 17 and TypeScript, and came with a 120,000-line package-lock.json. Of its five routes, four rendered the same 'coming-soon' page. Addtionally, If you hover over one of those boxes, they turn pink! If you ever hear me tell someone I am good at design, feel free to bring this up for discussion.

Back to plain HTML (Apr 2022)

Thankfully, I must've encountered motherfuckingwebsite sometime in early 2022. I got rid of React and went back to vanilla HTML and CSS. Unfortunately, I still didn't know how to make a real website landing page look great. So, while the React app was out, it was replaced with this beauty. Two hand-written pages set in Unica One and Open Sans. This stayed up until September 2023.

Clean slate (Jun 2026)

After a few more redesigns between 2023 and 2026, I felt I needed to reset my CSS. I had lost the plot. This reset helped me focus on figuring out what I truly wanted on a website, and put me on the path of iterating towards a design I truly enjoyed. Initially, everything was lowercase (which got annoying), and it was set in Ioskeley Mono. I then added a now page, a garden page, and a PGP key. I appreciate that my work here helped bring the design to where it is today.

Which brings us to now

There's an old misquote: "A good artist borrows, a great artist steals." I never really learned design, but I did learn how to steal. Every so often I would find a font I liked or some cool CSS on the web, and I'd bring it home to try on. Eventually I figured out what worked and what didn't, keeping the things I loved most.

So I wanted to acknowledge the people who's websites inspired me, and whose work I stole from.

  • The current iteration of the site is set in Geist Pixel, which I mercilessly ripped from royfish.dev after reading their excellent Fingerprints are the new cookies post.
  • I got the idea for themes from rmv.fyi. I visited Ruby's blog some time ago, and it shows a new color theme on every page load. I loved it. I then added themes to this site using color combinations from Flexoki by Steph Ango.
  • Comments, likes, and theme switcher in theme.js was written by an LLM. I’m counting that as stealing too.

I have also taken design, code, and ideas from these sites and developers, including many others I've certainly forgotten:

  • vale.rocks
  • textlog.cc
  • catskull.net
  • motherfuckingwebsite and its derivatives, like modernmotherfuckingwebsite

Thank you all.

I don’t know if this site is actually any better than my first version and I’ll probably want to redesign it again someday soon. But like that first one, I like it, I made (most of) it, and I’m proud.

- Daniel

entry.title: Wake Me Up When September Ends
entry.summary: The September 2026 now page. Starting the fall semester at Laney and applying to transfer, getting badly into home espresso, training for a half marathon, and notes on what I have been playing, reading, and listening to.
entry.content:
This page highlights what I've been doing recently. It updates on occasion, so check back every now and then, if you'd like. This is the september 2026 edition, 8 months on from my first update in January. The most current update can be found here.

College

This year, I finished the spring and summer semesters at Laney, a community college in Oakland, and I’m starting the fall semester. I’m taking Discrete Mathematics, Data Structures and Algorithms, and a history class—nothing too exciting.

What’s exciting is that next spring will be my final semester at community college before I transfer! I’m currently applying to transfer to a four-year university. My hope is to transfer to UC Santa Cruz for a B.S. in Computer Science. It’s also internship application season, so I’m hoping to pick up a summer software engineering internship next summer (if you know of any, please reach out!).

Life

I recently started getting into coffee. I’ve been making espresso at home and got addicted. I didn’t understand the coffee cult until recently, but drinking a warm espresso while reading the morning news on the balcony brings me so much joy each morning. I found a local coffee shop nearby called Mother Tongue. They have great beans, and it’s women-owned!

I also decided, for some reason, that I wanted to run a half marathon, so I’ve started training for it. yay.

Media

I’ve had less time for gaming lately, and I wish I had more positive notes on reading, but the music has been great.

Playing

  • REPLACED (3/5): a 2D platformer that’s absolutely gorgeous and perfect for the Steam Deck
  • Alan Wake 2: waiting for Spooky Season to really dive into it
  • the Dead Space Remake, if I have time

Reading

  • Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World (2/5) by Haruki Murakami
  • Carmilla (2/5) by Sheridan Le Fanu
  • A Court of Mist and Fury (2/5) by Sarah J. Maas
  • on to the next one -> Dungeon Crawler Carl

Listening

  • WOR$T GIRL IN AMERICA (5/5) (pop) from Slayyyter: amazing and perfect. It feels like this album was made specifically for me, and I’m so excited to see her live in concert soon!
  • Navy Blue (4/5) (alternative) by Porch Light, who will be releasing a new album, Hush, later this month

Watching

  • Widows Bay (5/5): if you’re into comedy or horror, I can’t recommend it enough. It’s fantastic.

I finally decided to put more effort into this site, so expect to see more frequent updates and changes in the near future! Come back soon

entry.title: Let Me Introduce Myself
entry.summary: Who I am: a software engineer and student in Oakland who went back to school to finish a computer science degree, and what I get up to otherwise — sci-fi and horror games, being outdoors, books, food, and learning French.
entry.content:
hi, I'm Daniel

I'm a software engineer and student living in Oakland, California. I worked professionally building backend services and data infrastructure before going back to school. College wasn't affordable for me the first time around, so I'm finishing my computer science degree now! I'm also learning video game development on the side

I built this site to practice writing, share my thoughts, and publish things I find interesting. It's mostly handwritten HTML and CSS - there's more on that here if you're interested.

my interests

If I'm not working, I'm probably enjoying one of the following activities!

Video games

I especially love sci-fi RPGs and horror. KOTOR 1 & 2, SWTOR, MASS EFFECT 1, 2, and 3 (and Andromeda!), Alan Wake 1 & 2, the Resident Evil series, and Dead Space are among my favorites. I've also played RuneScape since childhood and keep a rotating backlog of everything else.

Outdoors

I'm solar powered, so I enjoy almost anything that gets me outdoors and in the sun. I like to run, and occasionally will run races (see photo above). I also enjoy hiking, camping, kayaking, lifting, swimming, biking, and rock climbing.

Reading

Similar to games, I mainly enjoy science fiction and horror. I also enjoy fantasy and occasionally dip into non-fiction when I find a good one.

Food

I love great food and well-crafted cocktails. Banh Mi and ramen. Sourdough and butter. A cocktail and a small plate. Yellowbelly, Balkan Treat Box, and Menya Rui (St. Louis), Tall Boy and Bombera (Oakland), Tartine (SF - Manufactory), and Jane Jane (D.C.) are some of my favorite places - check them out!

French

I love the sound of it and am currently working on reading and speaking it. I hope to one day become fluent.

Say hello! Email me, especially if it's about books, food, or video games. My email is in the footer below.

entry.title: My First Now Page
entry.summary: The first now page. Two years into being Californians, weighing what the move gained and cost, and riding out the new-year feeling — plus what I was reading, listening to, and playing over winter.
entry.content:
This page highlights what I've been doing recently. It updates on occasion, so check back every now and then, if you'd like. This is the january 2026 edition. The most current update can be found here.

Christie and I just wrapped up our second year as Californians. We've been exploring California, trying to make new friends, and just settle into our new lives

california pros

  • consistent weather
  • access to national parks
  • redwoods

california cons

  • no snow, or fall :(
  • old friends are far away

Anyways, it's a new year and I'm trying to ride out that 'this year will be different' feeling for as long as possible. Just the usual stuff: more exercise, more reading, and maybe ease off some of the bad habits a little

Reading

Recently I was recommended "The Will of the Many" by James Islington, and I immediately devoured it. If you enjoy reading fantasy, this should be on your list

I was able to pick up a copy of book two, "The Strength of the Few", which released recently. It is also great, and every second I have to spend not reading it is pure agony. Highly recommend

Listening

I'm always actively hunting for new music, but right now it's going...okay... I find that the more I try new bands, or listen to new sounds, the more I need to ground myself in something familiar. So here is the new and the familiar

The new

  • tops - chlorine (indie pop)
  • olivia dean - dy-na-mi-tee (r&b - cover)
  • l'impératrice, louve - chrysalis (electronic french pop)

The familiar

  • lupe fiasco - kick, push (hip hop)
  • miguel ft j.cole - all i want is you (r&b)

Playing

I had extra time over winter break to go through a small backlog of games. KCD2 is a massive game, maybe too big. Demonschool was just not it for me. And I still don't quite know how to describe Indika

next up

  • alan wake 2

finished

  • kingdom come: deliverance ii by warhorse studios (4/5)
  • demonschool by necrosoft games (1/5)
  • indika by odd meter (3/5)

So here's to 2026
